title: Loops Practice
subject: Computer Science · Introduction to AI
instructions: Answer the three questions about for loops. Use the hints if you get stuck. Your teacher will review your work.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? Type the numbers separated by spaces.

misconceptions.note: Your loop counted from 1. Remember where range starts.
You included the stop number. Does range include it?

hints: Look at range(4). What is the first number it gives you? (Hint: the number inside range is where it stops.)
range(4) starts at 0 and stops before 4. Write down each value that i takes, one per turn around the loop.
A similar problem: for i in range(2): print(i) prints 0 and then 1 — two turns, and it never reaches 2. Now try range(4).

questions.prompt: How many times does the loop body run?

misconceptions.note: range(2, 7) does not include 7, but it does include 2.
The stop number is not the number of turns.

hints: range(2, 7) has a start and a stop. Where does it start, and where does it stop?
List the values one by one: it starts at 2 and stops before 7. Count how many values you wrote.
A similar problem: range(1, 4) gives 1, 2, 3 — that is 3 values. Try counting the values in range(2, 7) the same way.

questions.prompt: What number does this program print?
questions.code:
total = 0
for n in [3, 4, 5]:
    total = total + n
print(total)

misconceptions.note: That is how many items there are. What does total = total + n do each time?
The loop adds every item, not just the last one.

hints: Follow total step by step. What is total at the start, before the loop?
Turn 1 adds 3 to total. Turn 2 adds the next item. Write down total after each turn.
A similar problem: adding [1, 2] gives total 1 after the first turn and 3 after the second. Do the same steps for [3, 4, 5].
